# Luna stages with Terra evidence — 2026-11-13

Application commit **`f304747`**, unchanged from PY-054. Repeated Q02/Q04/Q07/Q08 once each, same questions, fifteen corpus/manifest hashes, all eleven stones, disposable stores, real local embeddings and limits. No retries or separate semantic judge.

## Experiment configuration

- Luna (`openai/gpt-6-luna`): parse, semantic grounding/audit, shortlist selection, answer.
- Terra (`openai/gpt-6.1-terra`): candidate/reference evidence extraction only.
- [Archived experiment-only harness](PY-055-evidence-model-harness.py.txt) overrides the structured model only for CandidateEvidence/ReferenceEvidence. Its SHA-256 matches the raw archive. The original harness is stored as archival text rather than an active Python module; raw metadata retains its original .py filename. No application code or permanent model-routing configuration changed.

The HTTP API shares one model setting between audit and evidence, so HTTP `model_ids` and runner `request_models` describe the shared Luna configuration. **Actual evidence overrides are separately recorded in `experiment.actual_stage_models`; exported generation telemetry confirms the executed model.** Do not infer Terra use from the HTTP request alone. The old runner's `FREE_MODEL_ID` variable was assigned Luna for this experiment; selection and answer are paid Luna, not a free model.

## Results against PY-054

| Case | Previous run | Current run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q02 | Luna grounding provider error; audit not measured | Parse correctly keeps resident granite contextual. Audit explicitly accepts built-in recommendation availability and marks complete. Luna selects candidates, then Terra evidence returns provider error → HTTP 500. |
| Q04 | Audit blocks missing candidate type and invented compatibility mandate | Same semantic errors; audit blocks again. Terra not reached. |
| Q07 | Luna grounding provider error | Candidate type and both agreement values represented. Invented compatibility mandate still exists and audit accepts it. Terra evidence returns provider error → HTTP 500. |
| Q08 | Incorrect mandate and false granite agreement values accepted; Sir Pebble excluded | Mandatory compatibility absent in this parse, but non-applicable scope still becomes false granite agreements. Luna grounding provider error; Terra not reached. |

**No end-to-end recommendation succeeded.** Two HTTP 200 responses contain refusals; Q02/Q07 return HTTP 500. The live capture test failed accordingly. Execution integrity: **0 pass / 2 fail / 2 unknown**, versus PY-054 1/3/0; these counts are not semantic answer-quality scores.

Q02 provides one positive observation for the availability audit clarification: the real audit accepts it. That does not establish a stable fix. Q04/Q07 demonstrate continuing context/mandatory-criterion confusion; Q08's different parse in one sample does not establish improvement.

## Terra and provider failures

Langfuse root matching recovered both HTTP-failure traces. Export contains **four traces, twelve generation observations**: ten Luna generations and **two Terra evidence generations, both ERROR: Provider returned error**. Q08 has a separate Luna grounding provider error. No completed Terra evidence output exists, so **this run cannot compare Terra versus Luna evidence accuracy**. The underlying provider causes are unknown; do not interpret the errors as Terra semantic failures.

Partial parser/audit outputs for HTTP-failure cases are recovered from generation telemetry in the comparison JSON, separately from missing final graph state. No raw application result was fabricated or replaced. No answer generation was reached in any case.

Reported generation cost: **$0.004681349999**; all twelve exported generations have cost fields. This is reported telemetry, not an independent billing reconciliation.
